questions.text: Given a hash table T with 25 slots that stores 2000 elements, the load factor [latex]\alpha[/latex] for T is ____________.
questions.solution:
Load factor [latex]\alpha=\frac{n}{m}=\frac{2000}{25}=80[/latex]

Answer: 80

questions.text: Consider a binary tree T that has 200 leaf nodes. Then, the number of nodes in T that have exactly two children are ________.
questions.solution:
In any binary tree, the number of nodes with two children = leaves [latex]-[/latex] 1.

200 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 199

Answer: 199

questions.text: Which one of the following hash functions on integers will distribute keys most uniformly over 10 buckets numbered 0 to 9 for i ranging from 0 to 2020?
questions.solution:
Last digit of [latex]i^3[/latex] for last digits 0..9: 0, 1, 8, 7, 4, 5, 6, 3, 2, 9. Every bucket gets used equally.

Squares end only in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 9, so options 1, 3, 4 leave some buckets empty.

Answer: h(i) = [latex]i^3[/latex] mod 10

questions.text:
With reference to the B+ tree index of order 1 shown below, the minimum number of nodes (including the Root node) that must be fetched in order to satisfy the following query:
"Get all records with a search key greater than or equal to 7 and less than 15"
is ____________.
questions.solution:
Search for 7: root (9) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] left internal node (5) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] leaf [5, 7].

Then follow leaf links: [9, 11] and [13, 15], where 15 shows we can stop.

Nodes = root + 1 internal + 3 leaves = 5

Answer: 5

questions.text: A binary tree T has 20 leaves. The number of nodes in T having two children is _______.
questions.solution:
In any binary tree, (nodes with 2 children) = (leaves) [latex]-[/latex] 1.

20 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 19

Answer: 19
